scenes.visual: Title card over the carried two-cell world using the first film's exact colour map: two identical touching cells side by side (left cell A, right cell B), each displaying warm amber ligands and cool teal Notch receptors along their shared border. High-contrast title: 'Equal Neighbours, Opposite Fates'. Gentle ambient shimmer along both membranes.

scenes.tts: In the first film, a neighbour's pull turned one Notch receptor into one nuclear signal. Now set two identical touching cells side by side: how do they pick opposite fates? Nothing outside tells them which cell becomes nerve and which cell becomes skin.
scenes.caption: In the first film, a neighbour's pull turned one Notch receptor into one nuclear signal. Now set two identical touching cells side by side: how do they pick opposite fates? Nothing outside tells them which cell becomes nerve and which cell becomes skin.
scenes.visual: Title fades; the two identical touching cells A (left) and B (right) expand to fill 65% of the frame height, with a blank schematic timeline strip below. Along their shared vertical wall, both cells carry matching warm amber ligands and cool teal Notch receptors. Small twin gauges inside each cell show equal amber 'Sending' and equal cyan 'NICD' levels, softly trembling.
scenes.narration: In the first film, a neighbour's pull turned one Notch receptor into one nuclear signal. Now set two identical touching cells side by side: how do they pick opposite fates? Nothing outside tells them which cell becomes nerve and which cell becomes skin.

scenes.tts: Both neighbours begin with the same toolkit. Each cell displays amber ligands to send and teal Notch receptors to receive. At the start, both pull equally on each other across their shared border. Neither cell has a lead, and neither cell has committed to a fate.
scenes.caption: Both neighbours begin with the same toolkit. Each cell displays amber ligands to send and teal Notch receptors to receive. At the start, both pull equally on each other across their shared border. Neither cell has a lead, and neither cell has committed to a fate.
scenes.visual: At the shared vertical wall, symmetric amber-to-teal links form in both directions. Equal faint pulses of cyan NICD drift into both cells' deep indigo nuclei, keeping both amber 'Sending' bars and both cyan 'NICD' bars level at the midpoint. Below, two overlapping traces (A and B) move horizontally together on a plot labelled 'Schematic ligand level'.
scenes.narration: Both neighbours begin with the same toolkit. Each cell displays amber ligands to send and teal Notch receptors to receive. At the start, both pull equally on each other across their shared border. Neither cell has a lead, and neither cell has committed to a fate.

scenes.tts: Then random chance gives the left cell slightly more ligand. It pulls harder on the right cell's Notch receptors, releasing more cyan inner tail into the right nucleus. There, in the textbook model, Notch turns on repressors with two linked jobs. They block the nerve programme, and they lower the right cell's own sending.
scenes.caption: Then random chance gives the left cell slightly more ligand. It pulls harder on the right cell's Notch receptors, releasing more cyan inner tail into the right nucleus. There, in the textbook model, Notch turns on repressors with two linked jobs. They block the nerve programme, and they lower the right cell's own sending.
scenes.visual: One extra warm amber ligand brightens on cell A's wall and tugs a teal Notch on cell B (brief gold lock peel, coral ADAM cut, violet γ-secretase cut). A brighter pulse of cyan NICD glides into cell B's nucleus, turning its gene emerald and releasing emerald repressor arcs that dim B's nerve icon and pull down B's amber 'Sending' gauge.
scenes.narration: Then random chance gives the left cell slightly more ligand. It pulls harder on the right cell's Notch receptors, releasing more cyan inner tail into the right nucleus. There, in the textbook model, Notch turns on repressors with two linked jobs. They block the nerve programme, and they lower the right cell's own sending.

scenes.tts: Pause here and follow the loop one step back across the border. The right cell now displays fewer amber ligands than before. What happens next to the Notch signal reaching the left cell, and to the left cell's own sending?
scenes.caption: Pause here and follow the loop one step back across the border. The right cell now displays fewer amber ligands than before. What happens next to the Notch signal reaching the left cell, and to the left cell's own sending?
scenes.visual: Hold both cells in place. Cell B's amber ligands along the shared wall visibly thin out and dim, while the arrow from B back to A's teal Notch pulses with a dotted question mark. Question card at top: 'Cell B sends less ligand: what happens to Cell A next?'
scenes.narration: Pause here and follow the loop one step back across the border. The right cell now displays fewer amber ligands than before. What happens next to the Notch signal reaching the left cell, and to the left cell's own sending?

scenes.visual: Hold the question card at top for 4.5 seconds while cell B's diminished amber ligands gently flicker and cell A's gauges wait in suspense. A thin progress bar sweeps smoothly across the bottom of the question card.

scenes.tts: With less ligand pulling on its Notch, the left cell receives less inhibition. Its nerve programme stays active, and it puts even more ligand on its surface. The left cell lowers the right cell's sending, and the right cell's sending lowers the left's. Two brakes in a row make positive feedback: quieting its neighbour boosts the left cell. When Notch lowers a cell's sending, equal neighbours split into opposite fates.
scenes.caption: With less ligand pulling on its Notch, the left cell receives less inhibition. Its nerve programme stays active, and it puts even more ligand on its surface. When Notch lowers a cell's sending, equal neighbours split into opposite fates.
scenes.visual: Question card fades. Inside cell A, cyan NICD fades downward and emerald repressors vanish; cell A's amber 'Sending' bar surges upward as fresh amber ligands populate its wall. A glowing circular double-inhibition loop arrow overlays the border ('A inhibits B -> B inhibits A less'), turning bright as the schematic traces below visibly begin to separate. Empathy fix: The loop label reads 'Left ⊣ right's sending ⊣ left's sending = left boosts left' (cell A is the left cell).
scenes.narration: With less ligand pulling on its Notch, the left cell receives less inhibition. Its nerve programme stays active, and it puts even more ligand on its surface. The left cell lowers the right cell's sending, and the right cell's sending lowers the left's. Two brakes in a row make positive feedback: quieting its neighbour boosts the left cell. When Notch lowers a cell's sending, equal neighbours split into opposite fates.

scenes.tts: Watch the schematic curves below pull apart as each cycle widens that tiny head start. Soon the left cell sends without receiving and adopts the nerve fate. The right cell receives without sending and adopts the skin fate. Biologists call this neighbour-sorting circuit lateral inhibition.
scenes.caption: Watch the schematic curves below pull apart as each cycle widens that tiny head start. Soon the left cell sends without receiving and adopts the nerve fate. The right cell receives without sending and adopts the skin fate. Biologists call this neighbour-sorting circuit lateral inhibition.
scenes.visual: The two traces on the 'Schematic ligand level' plot sweep cleanly apart: cell A's amber curve climbs high while cell B's curve drops near zero. Cell A glows warm amber labelled 'Sender: nerve', covered in amber ligands; cell B glows cool teal/emerald labelled 'Receiver: skin', displaying teal Notch and active emerald repressors. Banner fades gently at top: 'Lateral inhibition'.
scenes.narration: Watch the schematic curves below pull apart as each cycle widens that tiny head start. Soon the left cell sends without receiving and adopts the nerve fate. The right cell receives without sending and adopts the skin fate. Biologists call this neighbour-sorting circuit lateral inhibition.

scenes.tts: Now zoom out from one pair to a whole sheet of touching cells. Because the Notch signal neither diffuses nor multiplies, each cell compares itself only with the neighbours it contacts. Every emerging nerve precursor suppresses the ring of cells touching it, leaving spaced nerve cells surrounded by skin.
scenes.caption: Now zoom out from one pair to a whole sheet of touching cells. Because the Notch signal neither diffuses nor multiplies, each cell compares itself only with the neighbours it contacts. scenes.visual: Camera pulls back smoothly so cell A and cell B become two hexagons inside a 25-cell honeycomb sheet (labelled 'Schematic cell sheet'). Several scattered cells brighten to warm amber senders while each sender's immediate ring of touching neighbours turns cool teal/emerald receivers, producing a fine-grained salt-and-pepper mosaic with no two amber senders touching.
scenes.narration: Now zoom out from one pair to a whole sheet of touching cells. Because the Notch signal neither diffuses nor multiplies, each cell compares itself only with the neighbours it contacts. Every emerging nerve precursor suppresses the ring of cells touching it, leaving spaced nerve cells surrounded by skin.

scenes.tts: Cells can also tune that spacing without abandoning direct contact. On a fly's back, cells send out thin moving extensions that touch neighbours a few cell widths away. Live imaging shows these contacts help space the bristles, still using touch rather than diffusion.
scenes.caption: Cells can also tune that spacing without abandoning direct contact. On a fly's back, cells send out thin moving extensions that touch neighbours a few cell widths away. Live imaging shows these contacts help space the bristles, still using touch rather than diffusion.
scenes.visual: Zoom smoothly onto one warm amber sender in the schematic sheet. Thin, swaying amber membrane filaments extend outward past its nearest neighbours to brush teal Notch receptors two to three cell diameters away, turning a slightly wider ring of cells cool teal/emerald and spacing the next amber bristle precursor farther out. Label: 'Thin extensions (schematic)'.
scenes.narration: Cells can also tune that spacing without abandoning direct contact. On a fly's back, cells send out thin moving extensions that touch neighbours a few cell widths away. Live imaging shows these contacts help space the bristles, still using touch rather than diffusion.

scenes.tts: In flies and worms alike, this mutual brake turns a small starting gap into a clean choice. Two neighbours need no outside map and no diffusing signal. By weakening a neighbour's ability to send back, a tiny difference grows into two opposite fates.
scenes.caption: In flies and worms alike, this mutual brake turns a small starting gap into a clean choice. Two neighbours need no outside map and no diffusing signal. By weakening a neighbour's ability to send back, a tiny difference grows into two opposite fates.
scenes.visual: Smoothly blend back to the crisp amber sender beside the cool teal receiver in the honeycomb sheet, with a subtle amber-to-teal contact pulse maintaining the two opposite fates cleanly and steadily.
scenes.narration: In flies and worms alike, this mutual brake turns a small starting gap into a clean choice. Two neighbours need no outside map and no diffusing signal. By weakening a neighbour's ability to send back, a tiny difference grows into two opposite fates.

scenes.visual: Clean dark frame with subtle amber-and-teal accent line fading in. End card (one line only, no smaller line under it, large high-contrast white type): 'When Notch lowers a cell’s sending, equal neighbours split into opposite fates.'
